text:
evan: heads-up - docs PR #2501 (timeouts + streaming guide) is blocked. need runtime confirmation on timeout precedence and what happens to in-flight streaming responses when timeouts occur.

maria: what specifically is ambiguous in the PR?

evan: we document a global default timeout (30s) and route-level `timeout_ms`. the SDKs also show client-side timeouts in examples. reviewers want a clear precedence table and whether the server cancels generation on client disconnect or completes the job.

kai: runtime short answer: precedence = SDK client timeout (client-side) can abort the HTTP connection locally; route `timeout_ms` is enforced server-side and will cancel work at the runtime boundary; global default applies only when no route override. Order of authority: explicit SDK client timeout only affects client behavior (it does NOT change server route timeout). Server enforces route timeout regardless of client-side setting.

maria: ok, so if SDK timeout < route timeout, client closes connection but runtime may still be working. what does runtime do when it detects a closed connection?

kai: by default runtime cancels work when the client disconnects to avoid wasted cycles. The job is stopped and any partial generation is discarded unless route config sets `detach_on_client_disconnect=true` (experimental) which allows generation to finish and optionally write to cache.

docs-reviewer-lee: we need exact status codes/behaviors to doc. what does client observe if server cancels due to route timeout vs client abort?

kai: behaviors: - route timeout fired server-side: response is terminated with HTTP 408 Request Timeout and body JSON {"error":"timeout","timeout_ms":<ms>} if streaming, server will send a final "[STREAM_TERMINATED]" event then close. - client abort (SDK timed out locally and closed socket): server logs a client disconnect and returns no final HTTP response; SDK will surface a local timeout error. We recommend SDKs surface a consistent error (e.g., TimeoutError) and include whether it was client or server-side when detectable.

maria: do we have an SDK recommendation for keeping consistency? reviewers asked for a snippet.

sdk-bot: recommended SDK pattern: prefer to set client timeout slightly higher than route timeout if you want server to produce a final terminated stream; otherwise, client may cancel before server-side termination. Example comment: "Set client timeout >= route timeout to allow server-side timeout semantics to be observed by client."

evan: what's best practice for streaming apps that need partial results even if a timeout occurs?

kai: best practice: - use smaller incremental flushes from the server (shorter token batch windows) so clients receive partial tokens early. - if you need the server to finish even after client disconnect, enable `detach_on_client_disconnect=true` and write results to a durable store/caching layer. Note: detaching is experimental and has different cost profile.

docs-reviewer-lee: can you also clarify how `timeout_ms` interacts with model-level compute limits (like per-token budget)? for example, if model has internal safety cutoff earlier than route timeout.

kai: route `timeout_ms` is a hard cap applied by the runtime. If model-level compute finishes earlier, runtime returns as normal. If model enforces its own cutoff earlier due to safety, that is surfaced as normal completion with a note in response metadata. No extra timeout error is emitted unless route timeout is hit.

maria: CI note: add a short precedence bullet list and two tiny code snippets (JS + Python) showing: 1) client timeout < route timeout -> local abort, 2) client timeout >= route timeout -> server 408 visible. Also add the callout about `detach_on_client_disconnect` being experimental.

evan: I'll update the PR with wording and snippets. quick JS snippet idea: ```js
// prefer client timeout >= route timeout if you want server 408
fetch(url, {timeout: 35000}) // route timeout is 30s
```

maria: also add a short troubleshooting note: "If you see unexplained 408s, verify route timeouts and model cost patterns; if SDKs see local timeouts without server response, check client retries and network flakiness."

ci-bot: docs-preview: lint passed, linkcheck ok but flagged missing mention of experimental flag in migration notes.

evan: added experimental tag and a TODO to remove in GA. pushed.

docs-reviewer-lee: re-reviewing. if wording is explicit on precedence and snippets are present, I will approve.

ci-bot: docs-preview: all checks passed.

docs-reviewer-lee: approved. merging after you confirm final push.

evan: merging now. thanks for the quick answers!

kai: runtime note: no changes planned to timeout behavior this cycle. any change needs RFC and migration plan.
